committee: CC Commission for Persons with Disabilities
overview: The Medford Commission for Persons with Disabilities is a municipal advisory body tasked with promoting equal status, accessibility, and public resources for disabled residents across Medford. Operating continuously from July 2022 through September 2026 across three terms, the commission advises city officials and municipal departments on physical and digital compliance under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Its ongoing portfolio includes coordinating annual disability resource and pride fairs, reviewing accessibility in public parks and municipal facilities, advocating for transit and pedestrian infrastructure upgrades, and monitoring the city's comprehensive ADA transition plan. At its most recent meetings, the commission prioritized intersections for casino mitigation grant-funded accessible pedestrian signals and reviewed municipal facility and sidewalk surveys conducted by the Institute for Human Centered Design.

threads.name: Disability Fair and pride events
threads.summary: In early 2023, the commission initiated plans for an annual community disability pride event and resource fair, selecting the Brooks School for an inaugural October 2023 fair that hosted exhibitors and a mobile vaccine clinic [M05#4, M07#2, M11#3, M12#3]. Planning resumed in 2024 and 2025 to establish recurring dates, evaluate school venues such as the McGlynn School, and incorporate quiet rooms and accessibility accommodations [M16#3, M18#8, M19#2]. In May 2026, the commission hosted a Disability Pride and Culture Day fair featuring over 20 participating organizations and inclusive performances [M22#3, M23#4]. Following the event, commissioners reviewed participant feedback regarding signage and discussed adjusting hours or moving the event date when planning resumes in autumn [M23#4, M24#2].

threads.name: Public transit and rail accessibility
threads.summary: Early transit advocacy focused on regional access, including granting a variance for Wellington station restrooms and writing letters advocating for accessibility upgrades at the West Medford commuter rail station [M06#2, M07#6]. The body also addressed accessibility deficiencies at the newly opened Tufts Green Line Extension station, successfully coordinating the installation of dedicated accessible parking spaces [M11#6, M12#5]. The commission monitored grant awards and construction for the West Medford commuter rail ramp leading up to its opening in 2025 [M16#5, M18#4, M19#4]. Transit discussions continued into 2026, with the commission reviewing proposed MBTA bus route alterations with city transit officials [M24#4].

threads.name: Sidewalks, curb cuts, and pedestrian signals
threads.summary: The commission began tracking municipal pedestrian infrastructure in 2022, identifying non-navigable sidewalk paving along Fellsway West and a lack of curb cuts near key commercial intersections [M03#5]. The commission subsequently approved support for a municipal grant application prioritizing curb cuts near Medford High School and public spaces [M15#3]. Over subsequent sessions, members reviewed code enforcement trends regarding sidewalk snow obstructions and studied sidewalk tripping hazards caused by tree planting [M18#9, M22#7]. By 2026, the body partnered with Director of Traffic and Transportation Todd Blake to install accessible pedestrian signal buttons and prioritized candidate intersections for upgrades funded by a casino mitigation grant [M24#4, M25#3].

threads.name: Parks and playground accessibility
threads.summary: The commission partnered with consultant Chenine Peloquin to evaluate inclusive playground standards and advocate for accessible paths and restrooms, focusing initial efforts on Carr Park [M12#6, M13#3]. Commissioners continued monitoring park projects by consulting on accessible designs for the McGlynn school play space and reviewing school Gaga pit accessibility [M18#5, M20#5]. The body contributed community survey feedback regarding park accessibility barriers to inform the city's Open Space and Recreation Plan extension [M20#8]. In 2026, the commission reviewed design proposals for the Tufts Park redesign, offering recommendations on accessible pathways, restrooms, dog separation, and screen-reader survey access [M23#2].

threads.name: Municipal buildings and facility upgrades
threads.summary: Early facility work targeted ADA deficiencies at Medford High School, including non-compliant entrances, speed bump obstacles, and obstructed curb cuts [M03#6, M05#4]. The commission voted to support appointing a commissioner to the Medford High School Building Committee to ensure ongoing accessibility oversight [M15#2]. In City Hall, the commission used ARPA funding to acquire accessible parking stencils, assistive listening receivers, and cushioned armchairs for public chambers [M04#4, M18#3, M19#3]. The commission also reviewed elevator repairs and tracked progress on the design phase for fully accessible public restrooms in City Hall [M18#7, M19#3, M20#5].

threads.name: ADA transition plan and self-evaluation surveys
threads.summary: The city initiated an ADA self-evaluation study supported by municipal grant funding [M22#6]. The Institute for Human Centered Design was retained to perform physical audits of municipal facilities, beginning with an evaluation of City Hall [M23#6, M24#3]. Work expanded across 2026 to include surveys of broader municipal structures and sidewalks alongside an application for implementation grant funding [M24#3, M25#2]. In late 2026, the commission reviewed the progress of these structural surveys while raising accessibility concerns regarding the institute's digital communications [M25#2].

threads.name: Commission ordinance and governance
threads.summary: Commissioners distributed the municipal ordinance governing the body in 2023 to evaluate options for modernizing its structure and operations [M08#5]. Discussions continued across multiple terms regarding updating the commission's name and reviewing its mandate to ensure equal political status for people with disabilities [M11#8, M12#4, M17#5]. In 2026, the City Council approved forwarding a proposed updated ordinance to the mayor for legal review [M21#5]. Staff later confirmed that the revised ordinance was completing legal review for City Council consideration [M23#6].

threads.name: Polling place and elections accessibility
threads.summary: The commission coordinated with city staff in 2022 to add an accessible voting link to the city website [M03#9]. Ahead of subsequent elections, commissioners planned site visits to verify that accessible voting machines were functional, appropriately positioned, and operated by trained staff [M17#4]. The body reviewed testing and calibration updates from the elections department while discussing alternative voting methods [M20#9]. Review of voting machine accessibility testing continued through mid-2026 [M23#7].
